title: Exodus close: chazak
hook: slaves have become a people with a law and a sanctuary

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last verse of Exodus: the cloud of the Lord over the sanctuary, in all their journeys. Your line was cloud by day, fire by night. Today, the book closes.

On the Shabbat when the last verse of Exodus is read aloud, something happens in Ashkenazi synagogues that happens only when a book of the Torah ends. The reader chants the final words, in all their journeys, and before the next word can be spoken, the whole room calls out together, loud: chazak, chazak, v'nitchazek. Children shout it. People who've been half dozing sit up and say it. Then the reader repeats it. There are five books, so it comes five times in the yearly reading. Today, Exodus ends, and it's your turn.
screen: `THE LAST VERSE IS READ.` → `THE ROOM CALLS OUT TOGETHER.` → `FIVE TIMES A YEAR.`

segments.voice: Chazak means be strong. Chazak, chazak, v'nitchazek: be strong, be strong, and let us be strengthened. That's the Ashkenazi custom; in Sephardi synagogues the reader is often greeted with chazak u'varuch, be strong and blessed. Why strength, at the end of a book? One reason people give is that finishing is exactly when you need it, to keep going into the next book. The word echoes what Moses and God tell Joshua when he takes over: be strong and of good courage. And look what Exodus has carried. The medieval commentator Ramban called it the book of exile and redemption, and said the redemption isn't complete when the people leave Egypt, or even at Sinai. It's complete when God's presence rests among them, which is exactly how the book ends. Since this year began, you've walked the second half of the story: the last plagues and the first Passover, the sea, the manna, Sinai and the ten words, the laws of Mishpatim, the gifts of Terumah, the priest's clothes in Tetzaveh, the golden calf and the thirteen attributes in Ki Tisa, and the building in Vayakhel and Pekudei. This week: no fire on Shabbat, an open account, as the Lord commanded, Moses blessing the workers, the cloud filling the tent, the journeys. The book began with slaves building cities for Pharaoh. It ends with a free people who built something else, together, for God, and a cloud over it.
screen: `CHAZAK: BE STRONG.` · `AND LET US BE STRENGTHENED.` · `RAMBAN: EXILE AND REDEMPTION.` · `FROM PHARAOH'S CITIES TO A SANCTUARY.` · then, large: `BE STRONG, BE STRENGTHENED.`

segments.voice: Think back over Exodus, the sea, the mountain, the calf, the cloud, and hold the moment that stayed with you most for a few breaths. Then, out loud if you can, even quietly, say the words the synagogue says: chazak, chazak, v'nitchazek. Notice that it says us.
Chazak. Be strong — called out together when a book of the Torah ends, as the room finishes Exodus with chazak, chazak, v'nitchazek.
Your line: be strong, be strengthened. One book closes, and the next one waits. Day three hundred seventy-eight.

chat.says: Why does everyone shout chazak when they finish reading a book of the Torah?
options: It means be strong; finishing is when you need strength to keep going into the next book.
It means it's finished; people shout it so the reader knows to close the scroll.
It's a signal to stand, because the next book is always read standing.
